reasons: The file only holds a description, so there is nothing to test.

terms.meaning: a folder of Python code that other code can import by name

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Package description line
sections.what: Holds a one-line description of the parsers folder. It does not change how the app behaves.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

summary: Marks the parsers folder as a Python package and contains only a one-line description.
purpose: Lets other parts of the app import the document parsers from this folder by name.
why: Likely reason: Python needs this file, even when it is nearly empty, to treat the folder as an importable package. Reason not stated for the description line.
how: Python reads this file when something first imports the parsers folder. It does nothing else because it contains no code.
outputs: None. It creates no objects or values.
risks: Low. Nothing here can fail. If imports are added here later, every parser would load at once, which slows startup.
debug: If an import of a parser fails, look at the parser file itself, not this file.
